@about: Interior lighting design add-on (0.9 LD). Words of the add-on only; the engine has none. Other languages fall back to English until the next translation run.
name: Interior lighting design
intro: Light a room from the luminaires' photometry files: the mean, lowest and highest lux on the workplane, uniformity, glare, walls and ceiling, and watts per square metre, with the light bounced off the room's surfaces. A design aid: check it against the standard and your own judgement.
host.none: This app has no rooms or drawing to read from. Type the outline below.
room.none: No closed shapes found. Select one, or type the outline below.
room.outline: Outline (x, y in millimetres, one corner per line)
lum.generic: A typical figure for this kind of luminaire, not a maker's: load the maker's file for a real design.
mode.plan.note: Finds the fewest luminaires, in an even grid, that reach the mean lux (and uniformity) you type.
mode.grid.note: Luminaires in an even grid: one in the middle of each cell of the room.
mode.rows.note: Rows of luminaires, evenly spread, along the room's x or y direction.
mode.landscape.note: The lights the landscape asks for: an up-light at the foot of each tree, a bollard every 5 m along each path, a pole at each marked spot. Each uses its own generic type, not the luminaire chosen above.
mode.landscape.facts: In this area: {trees} trees, {paths} paths, {spots} spots.
preset.workshop.medium: Workshop: medium bench and machine work
draw.done: Drew {n} luminaires and the lux values.
map.alt: Lux on the workplane, dark blue lowest to yellow highest, luminaires as white dots
map.note: Lux on the workplane: dark blue lowest, yellow highest ({max} lx).
note.model: Direct light from the luminaires' photometry plus the light bounced off floor, walls and ceiling as diffuse reflectors. No furniture, columns or inner walls block light, no windows or daylight: a room that is not a simple box is a little too bright in its bays.
note.llf: Lux are maintained values: the light loss factor is applied to every figure.
note.ugr: UGR is an estimate from the CIE 117 formula with the luminaires' candela and luminous opening, at initial flux, for four observers at 1.2 m: compare it with the maker's own UGR table.
note.opening: A photometry file gave no luminous opening, so 0.1 × 0.1 m was assumed for the glare figure.
err.room: The outline needs at least three corners that enclose some area.
err.height: The ceiling height must be between 0.5 and 60 m.
err.workplane: The workplane must be below the ceiling.
err.noluminaires: There are no luminaires to calculate.
err.empty: No luminaire falls inside the room: change the layout.
err.nolandscape: No tree, path or spot of the landscape falls inside this area: choose another area or another layout.
err.nogrid: The room is too small for a calculation grid.
err.plan: Type a mean lux to plan for, and use a luminaire with a lumen figure.
err.plan.max: No even grid of up to 400 luminaires reaches that. The best one tried: {n} luminaires, {em} lx. Choose a stronger luminaire or lower the target.
err.file: That file could not be read.
photo.ies.nofile: That is not an IES file.
photo.ies.notilt: The IES file has no TILT line.
photo.ies.tilt: The IES file's TILT data could not be read.
photo.ies.numbers: The IES file's numbers could not be read.
photo.ies.counts: The IES file's angle counts are not usable.
photo.ies.type: Only photometric type C IES files are read (this one is type {type}).
photo.ies.short: The IES file ends before its candela table does.
photo.ies.angles: The IES file's angles are not in order.
photo.ies.hangles: The IES file's horizontal angles are not a layout we read.

photo.ldt.header: That EULUMDAT file's header could not be read.

photo.ldt.numbers: That EULUMDAT file's angles could not be read.
photo.ldt.planes: That EULUMDAT file's planes do not start at C0.

bim.label: Lighting design luminaires
day.note: Daylight alone, under the standard overcast sky: how much of the light outside reaches the workplane through the windows. No ground reflection, no buildings or trees outside, no sun.
day.windows: Windows (one per line: wall, from, width, sill, head, glass transmittance; the wall is the one from corner 0 to 1 as 0, 1 to 2 as 1, and so on; millimetres)
day.target: Show how much of the room reaches a daylight factor of
obs.boxes: Boxes that block direct light (one per line: x0, y0, x1, y1, z0, z1 in millimetres)
em.every: Every n-th luminaire is on the emergency circuit, n =
em.share: Output in an emergency, as a share of rated lumens
em.route: Escape route (x, y in millimetres, one point per line)
em.ratio: Route, highest to lowest at most
day.share: {p} % of the workplane reaches a daylight factor of {df} % or more.
day.dropped: {n} window(s) did not fit their wall or the room's height and were left out.
em.facts: {n} of {of} luminaires on the emergency circuit, at {share} % of their rated output.
note.daylight: Daylight: the CIE standard overcast sky, the window cut into small cells, the light that comes in bounced between the room's surfaces. No ground reflection, no buildings, trees or overhangs outside, no sun; the glass passes the same share of light at every angle; no frames, bars or curtains.
note.daylight2: The window opening lets light out as well, so the wall behind the glass reflects none. A daylight factor is daylight alone: it is not added to the electric light above.
note.obstruct: Furniture and partitions block the direct light only; bounced light passes through them. Points inside a box are left out. Behind a box the room reads a little too bright, never too dark.
note.emergency: Emergency lighting: direct light on the floor from the luminaires on the emergency circuit only, at their emergency output. Light bounced off walls and ceiling is ignored.
note.emergency2: The limits are typical values in the style of EN 1838, not checked against the current edition and waiting for a lighting engineer. Signs, duration and switch-over time are not checked.
err.nowindows: No window fits: check the wall number, position and height.
err.noemergency: No luminaire is on the emergency circuit.
err.win.edge: Window on a wall the room does not have
err.win.fit: Window does not fit along its wall
err.win.height: Window height does not fit the room
err.win.t: Glass transmittance must be above 0 and at most 1
bim.noroom: This room is not one of the model's rooms any more: read the rooms again and pick it.
bim.draw.label: Place lighting design luminaires
bim.erase.label: Remove lighting design luminaires
bim.lux.label: Lighting design lux on the plan
draw.done.bim: Placed {n} light fixtures in the model and {lux} strokes of lux numbers in the plan view.
f.outdoor: Outdoors: site lighting (no ceiling or walls; direct light on the ground)
note.site: Site lighting: the lux are the direct light of the luminaires on the ground, with no light bounced back from the ground, buildings or trees. Buildings and trees you list shade it. The night picture does show some bounced light, so it can look a little brighter than the numbers.
webs.cap: More than 32 different photometry files: the rest are drawn in the night picture as plain lamps without their measured light spread.
night.note.room: The picture is the room from the outline, lit by the luminaires above (their measured light spread, lumens and colour temperature) and nothing else, drawn by the renderer's reference path tracer on this page. The false-colour view beside it gives the lux on the workplane from the same calculation as the table. It is not your model.
night.note.site: The picture is the site from the outline at night, lit by the luminaires above (their measured light spread, lumens and colour temperature) and nothing else, drawn by the renderer's reference path tracer on this page. The false-colour view beside it gives the lux on the ground from the same calculation as the table. It is not your model.
night.facts: {n} lamps, {w} measured light spreads, exposure {e} stops
night.note.model: The picture is the room as the model has it (its walls, floors, ceilings and what stands in it, in the colours of the 3D view), lit by the luminaires above (their measured light spread, lumens and colour temperature) and nothing else, drawn by the renderer's reference path tracer on this page. The false-colour view beside it gives the lux on the workplane from the same calculation as the table, which uses the outline and its reflectances, not the model's colours.
night.model: Drawn with the model's own surfaces ({n} triangles near the room).
night.model.nofloor: The model has no floor under the room: the outline's floor is used.
night.model.noceiling: The model has no ceiling over the room: the outline's ceiling is used.
night.model.height: The model's ceiling over the room is at {z} mm, the calculation's at {h} mm: the lamps in the picture hang under the model's ceiling. Type {z} as the ceiling height and calculate again so the numbers match the picture.
night.nokit: This app has no renderer, so only the false-colour view is drawn. Open the design in BimCraft for the night picture, or take the lamps file to a render.
night.false: False colour: lux on the workplane or ground, brighter toward red
cat.where: Where to get files: luminaire makers publish a photometry file (EULUMDAT .ldt or IES .ies) for each product, usually on the product's page or in the maker's download area. Save the ones you use in a folder and add the folder here. Nothing is sent anywhere: the files stay in this app's storage on this device.
cat.empty: No catalogue yet: add files or a folder and one is made.
cat.unsaved: This catalogue is too big for this app's storage: it is kept until the page closes. Split it into smaller catalogues to keep it.
cat.sort.name: Name
cat.more: The first {n} are shown: narrow the search to see the rest.
cat.none: The catalogue luminaire is not there any more: pick another one.
cat.beamnote: Names, makers, lumens and watts are what each file says. The beam is worked out here: the angle between the directions where the light falls to half its peak, the mean of the C0 and C90 planes; "wide" when it never falls that far.
v3d.show: Show the lux as a 3D surface
v3d.alt: The workplane lux as a 3D surface, {min} to {max} lx
v3d.note: Height and colour are the lux at each grid point ({min} to {max} lx, the colours of the map); height starts from 0 lx on the floor, so an even room is a raised, nearly flat sheet. Dashed lines drop from its corners to the floor. Drag the picture to turn it. Dots are the luminaires, on the floor outline.
mod.noroom: Select one floor face in the model, then read the rooms again.

mod.erase.label: Lighting design: remove luminaires
mod.surface.label: Lighting design: lux surface
draw.done.model: {n} luminaires placed as bodies in the model{s}.
road.on: Road lighting (a road or street instead of a room)
road.intro: A straight road: its cross-section, the luminaires along it, and the field between two neighbouring luminaires. You get illuminance on the carriageway and footways, the road-surface luminance and its uniformities from a reflection table you paste, the threshold increment, the edge illumination ratio, and checks against the class values you enter. A design aid: check every result against your class table.
road.none: No roads in this project: type the cross-section below.
road.section: Cross-section, left edge to right edge, one strip a line (kind, width in m, and for a carriageway the number of lanes and "one-way" if it is)
road.section.note: Kinds: carriageway, footway, cycleway, verge, median. On a two-way carriageway the left half of the lanes run the other way. Footways and cycleways get their own illuminance grid.
road.arr.note: Overhang is how far the luminaire reaches over the carriageway from its edge (negative: set back behind it); twin arms reach that far each way from the middle of the median, or the middle of the road when there is none. Tilt turns the luminaire towards the road. The file is read with C 90° pointing out over the road and C 0° along it; if your file is the other way, turn it by 90° or 180°.
road.across: Points across each lane or strip
road.grid.note: The grid is yours to set: type the spacing your standard asks for. Points sit in the middle of their cells. The defaults (10 along, 3 across a lane) are ours, not a standard's.
road.rtable: Reflection table (r × 10 000), pasted from your standard's table or a measured surface: first line the tan γ values, then one line a β angle (degrees) with its values
road.rtable.none: No reflection table: the luminance, its uniformities, the threshold increment and the veiling luminance ratio are not worked out. The add-on ships no road surface table.
road.rtable.ok: Reflection table read: {b} β angles × {n} tan γ values (up to tan γ {max}).
road.rt.short: The reflection table needs a line of tan γ values and at least two β lines.
road.rt.tans: The first line must be the tan γ values, rising from 0 (at most 40).
road.rt.row: Line {n} of the reflection table does not have one β and a value for every tan γ.
road.rt.betas: The β angles must rise and stay within 0 to 180 degrees.
road.rt.neg: A reflection table value cannot be negative.
road.rt.big: The reflection table has more than 40 β lines.
road.err.rtable: The reflection table could not be read: see the note under it.
road.set.rp8: RP-8-00 illuminance table (as reproduced by FHWA)
road.src.own: Type the values from your standard's class table. 0 = not checked.
road.src.s.m: Values from K. Sørensen, "Road lighting" (NMF, 2013), Table 2 p. 16, which reproduces the EN 13201-2 M classes. The standard lets a country amend Ul, TI and EIR: check against your class table and edition. Wet-road Uo is not checked.
road.src.s.c: Values from K. Sørensen, "Road lighting" (NMF, 2013), Table 3 p. 16 (EN 13201-2 C classes, as reproduced there). Check against your class table and edition.
road.src.s.p: Values from K. Sørensen, "Road lighting" (NMF, 2013), Table 4 p. 17 (EN 13201-2 P classes, as reproduced there); the average may not be more than 1.5 times the class value (its note a). Check against your class table and edition.
road.src.rp8: Values from FHWA-HRT-14-051 (2014), Table 20, which reproduces the ANSI/IES RP-8-00 illuminance criteria. Later RP-8 editions differ: check against the edition you work to.
road.chk.claim: These checks compare numbers. They are not a claim that the road meets a standard: check against your class table.
road.facts: {n} luminaires a field of {s} m; grid {along} × {across} a lane (points {d} m apart along); maintenance factor {llf}. Illuminance and luminance are maintained; the threshold increment uses initial values.
road.r.nol: not worked out: no reflection table
road.r.obs: observer in lane {n}: L {l}, Uo {uo}, Ul {ul}
road.plan.note: The field (blue frame) and half a spacing each side, seen from above: colour is the illuminance (blue low, red high), dots are luminaires.
road.plan.alt: Plan of the road field with the illuminance grid and the luminaires
road.note.straight: A straight, level road: curves, junctions, roundabouts and slopes are not modelled.
road.note.grid: The grid is the one typed above; the observer for luminance stands in the middle of each lane, 60 m before the field, eyes 1.5 m up (Sørensen 2013, p. 74).
road.note.direct: Direct light only: no light reflected from buildings, trees or other surfaces.
road.note.nortable: No reflection table, so no luminance, Ul, threshold increment or veiling luminance ratio.
road.note.ti: Threshold increment TI = 65 Lv / L^0.8 from initial values, Lv = K Σ E/θ² at an eye 1.5 m up looking 1° down, luminaires up to 500 m ahead and below a 20° roof line (Sørensen 2013, pp. 94-95). The eye illuminance is taken on a plane facing along the line of sight: our reading.
road.note.claim: Not a compliance certificate: check against your class table and the edition of the standard you must meet.
road.prob.unknown: {area}: {what} could not be worked out (no reflection table)
